sentences.text: 1  JUDGMENT & ORDER (ORAL)
Heard Mr. P. Roy Barman, learned senior counsel assisted by Mr. Samarjit Bhattacharjee, learned counsel for the petitioners.

[2] The present writ petition has been filed by the petitioners, Sri Subhash Debnath and Abinash Debnath, son of late Jogendra alias Jogesh Chandra Debnath the original awardee in LA Case No.01/ MNP/2020 in respect of which notice under sub-section (1) of 3H of The National Highways Act, 1956 was issued upon the awardees, namely, Rayati Chitta Debnath, son of Amarchand Debnath, Jogendra Chandra Debnath, son of Sashimohan Debnath and Umesh Chandra Debnath, son of Sashimohan Debnath of Mohanpur and one unregistered deed occupier Ram Kumar Das, son of Mahananda Das asking them to get compensation towards awarded value of Rs.77,19,974/-.

Petitioners alleged that instead of disbursement of 1/3rd share of the award in favour of the petitioners, who are legal heirs of the original awardee Jogendra Chandra Debnath, son of Sashimohan Debnath, the entire amount has been disbursed to Sri Sishu Debnath,
son of Umesh Chandra Debnath, Sri Champak Debnath, son of Sribash Debnath and Sri Chitta Debnath, son of Amarchand Debnath vide letter No.9766/70 dated 18.06.2021 (Annexure-6) issued by the competent authority/Additional District Magistrate & Collector, West Tripura in connection with the same LA case.

It is however also pointed out that the letter No.9766/70 dated 18.06.2021 shows that it is on the subject of Correction of Award No.10/NH-108B/20 dated 18.12.2020 under apportionment serial No.9/p & 9(A) of L.A Case No.1/MNP/2020 at Mouja Taranagar, Sheet No.5/p in respect of acquisition of land for upgradation of NH-108B from Agartala-Khowai under Mohanpur Sub-Division.

[3] Petitioners contend that they have a survival certificate issued by Sub-Divisional Magistrate,
Mohanpur, West Tripura dated 31.12.2021 on death of their father (Annexure-3).

Though no partition deed was made against the Rayati co-sharer in Khatian No.1496 but share of Ramesh Chandra Debnath was transferred to one Chitta Debnath, son of late Amar Chand Debnath by way of sale and for this reason in the finally published computerized Khatian No.1496, name of Ramesh Chandra Debnath was replaced by Chitta Debnath as co-sharer along with two others of late Jogendra alias Jogesh Chandra Debnath and Umesh Chandra Debnath of land measuring 2.18 acres recorded as joint owner and possessor of the said land.

It is submitted that for upgradation of the NH-108B in the concerned section of Agartala-Khowai road, notice was issued on 09.12.2020 to the owners of Khatian No.1496 for acquisition of portions of their land i.e. plot Nos.8808, 8809/P and 8803/P classified as tilla, measuring 0.09, 0.02 and 0.8799999 acres respectively (Annexure- 4).

Pursuant to the said notice, the award was published by the competent authority i.e. Additional District Magistrate & Collector, West Tripura amounting to Rs.77,19,974/- to the three Rayati land owners and one unregistered deed occupier-Ram Kumar Das, son of Mahananda Das.

entities.text: Additional District Magistrate & Collector, West Tripura, Agartala
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As such, the petitioners have been compelled to approach this Court invoking the writ jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

[4] On consideration of the submission of learned senior counsel for the petitioners and the material facts and documents enclosed to the writ petition, it appears that under the provisions of Section 3H of The National Highways Act, 1956, after determination of the amount payable as compensation in terms of section 3G in respect of the acquired land vide notification issued under 3D thereof the competent authority is required to pay the awarded amount deposited by the Central Government to the person or persons entitled thereto.

Under sub-section (3) where several persons claim to be interested in the amount deposited under sub- section (1) the competent authority shall determine the persons who in its opinion are entitled to receive the amount payable to each of them.

Under sub-section (4) if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

[5] Petitioners herein alleged that the competent authority has disbursed the entire awarded amount though petitioners being legal heirs of late Jogesh alias Jogendra Chandra Debnath, one of the awardees, was entitled to 1/3rd of the share.
Any correction of award has been made behind their back without notice.
This evidently gives rise to a dispute as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable.

In terms of Section 3H sub-section (4) when in such an event the competent authority has to refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

[6] Petitioners have approached this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India however, before raising the dispute relating to apportionment of the amount to the persons,
namely, Sri Sishu Debnath, son of Umesh Chandra Debnath, Sri Champak Debnath, son of Sribash Debnath and Sri Chitta Debnath, son of Amarchand Debnath vide letter dated 18.06.2021 (Annexure-6).

As such, at this stage, in a dispute relating to apportionment of the original award amongst the legal heirs of the original awardees and certain other persons in whose name the amount has been disbursed vide letter No.9766/70 dated 18.06.2021 (Annexure-6), it would be appropriate to direct the petitioners to approach the competent authority i.e. the Additional District Magistrate & Collector, West Tripura, Agartala under whose authority the award has been prepared and notice was also issued upon the awardees vide letter dated 09.12.2020 (Annexure-4).

in accordance with law, of course after giving due notice to the other parties in favour of whom the award has been disbursed.
